intro: Phnom Penh rewards visitors with grand royal palaces, sobering history, and a buzzing riverside food scene. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: No metro or tram; the city bus network has 13 lines running about 05:30-20:30.
City bus fare is 1,500 riel per ride; drivers give no change, so pay exact.
Tuk-tuks cost about US$2-3 in town and US$8 to the airport; agree the fare first.
Ride apps PassApp, Grab and TADA work well and show fixed prices, so no haggling.
Motorbikes rent for US$5-6 a day; traffic is chaotic and theft is common, so park in guarded areas.
Cyclos and bicycles are slow but scenic; bike hire is US$1-3 a day.

royal-palace.name: Royal Palace of Cambodia
royal-palace.price_text: ≈ KHR 40,000 (check on the day; camera fee may apply)
royal-palace.hours: Daily roughly 08:00–11:00 and 14:00–17:00 · closed on some royal holidays
royal-palace.tip: Dress modestly — cover shoulders and knees — and go at opening to beat the heat and crowds.

tuol-sleng.name: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum
tuol-sleng.price_text: ≈ KHR 20,000 plus optional audio guide (check on the day)
tuol-sleng.tip: Take the audio guide; the site is heavy, so allow quiet time afterwards.

killing-field.name: Killing Field (Choeung Ek)
killing-field.price_text: ≈ KHR 20,000 plus optional audio guide (check on the day)
killing-field.tip: It is about 15 km out of town — agree a tuk-tuk round trip and price before you go.

wat-phnom.name: Wat Phnom
wat-phnom.tip: Climb the hill in the late afternoon for shade and a breeze.

national-museum.name: National Museum of Cambodia
national-museum.tip: The shaded courtyard is a calm break between the palace and the riverside.

mekong-river.name: Mekong River waterfront
mekong-river.price_text: Free to walk; sunset cruises cost extra
mekong-river.tip: Walk the Sisowath Quay promenade at sunset, then eat nearby.

independence-monument.name: Independence Monument of Cambodia
independence-monument.tip: Best seen after dark when it is floodlit — a quick photo stop.

phsar-thmei.name: Phsar Thmei (Central Market)
phsar-thmei.price_text: Free to enter; pay per item
phsar-thmei.tip: The art-deco dome is worth the visit alone; bargain politely.

phsar-toul-tom-poung.name: Phsar Tuol Tom Poung (Russian Market)
phsar-toul-tom-poung.price_text: Free to enter; pay per item
phsar-toul-tom-poung.tip: Come hungry for the food stalls and go early before it gets stifling.

fish-amok.name: Fish Amok (national dish)
fish-amok.hours: Lunch and dinner at most Khmer restaurants
fish-amok.tip: Try it at a local Khmer restaurant rather than a tourist menu for a fresher version.

riverside-walk.name: Sisowath Quay riverside walk
riverside-walk.tip: Stroll north from the palace end at sunset for the liveliest stretch.

sunset-cruise.name: Mekong sunset boat cruise
sunset-cruise.hours: Departures late afternoon to early evening
sunset-cruise.tip: Confirm the departure point and price on the quay before boarding.

bkk1-food.name: BKK1 café and restaurant streets
bkk1-food.tip: Good for a modern coffee stop or a mix of Khmer and international food.

tonle-bassac-walk.name: Tonle Bassac neighbourhood walk
tonle-bassac-walk.tip: A quieter area to wander; keep valuables close and stick to busy streets.

cyclo-tour.name: Cyclo city tour
cyclo-tour.tip: Agree the route and total price before you set off.

night-market.name: Riverside night market
night-market.tip: Come for cheap street food and a lively evening atmosphere.

stays.why: Walk to the Royal Palace, night market and riverside bars; most tuk-tuks and restaurants are on your doorstep.
Quiet streets right by the main sights and the National Museum; good for early starts before the heat.
Modern cafés, embassies and mid-range hotels; a short ride from the sights and the best food street in town.
Newer high-rises and malls near the Independence Monument; calm nights and easy ride-app pickups.

food: Start the day with kuy teav (rice-noodle soup) or bai sach chrouk (grilled pork and rice) at a street stall; expect a few thousand riel.
Try fish amok (coconut curry steamed in a banana leaf) and lok lak (stir-fried beef with lime-pepper dip) at a mid-range Khmer restaurant.
Eat at the evening food stalls and night market near the riverside; point at what looks busy and pay in small riel notes.
Drink only bottled or filtered water, and be careful with ice from street carts; hotel and restaurant ice is usually fine.
Vegetarian and halal options are easy to find around BKK1 and the riverside; ask before ordering fish sauce or prahok.
more_time: Add a half-day to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum and the Killing Fields of Choeung Ek; go early, it is emotional and hot.
Take a slow boat or bus to Siem Reap for Angkor Wat if you have two spare days; check times and tickets on the day.
Cross the river to Areyksat for a quiet half-day of village lanes and river views, a short ferry ride from the city.
